referenceHeightMethod: For each bearing independently, take the exact half-up median of all four contact cap-to-nearer-support-sole alpha>=64 native spans. Apply that one reference unchanged to both contact and casualty sources. SE [435,391,420,404] gives412; NW [404,381,373,383] gives382. No phase-specific, casualty-specific or borrowed normalization.
rootMethod: Native rounded integer projected pelvis/hip X is selected from anatomy and need not lie inside the support ROI. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 maximum Y of the explicitly named supporting sole, knee/hip or forearm/hand region; lifted soles, overhead arms and released weapons are excluded.

sourceWideDecisions.se: Contact guard/low thrust/recovery/high parry and casualty hit/knee/collapse/ground-rest preserve B front-three-quarter SE kit. Head, pack, limbs and boots are sufficiently coherent for one shared reference despite natural projection differences. Final rest is non-aiming.
sourceWideDecisions.nw: Rear NW contact and attempt8 casualty retain B left canteen, brown pouch, strapped pack/roll and coherent head/limb/boot proportions. Attempt8 cap79px and planted boot75px compare with83px each in contact phase0; multi-part visual inspection resolves the material enlargement from attempt6. The final pose lowers head/forearms and leaves the rifle separately grounded.

cellObservations.observation: SE front-three-quarter low guard. Both hands meet the rifle at plausible separated grip points; brown pouches/boots, navy coat, light blue trousers and rolled blanket preserve B identity.
Distinct two-handed low extension and weight transfer into a bent forward leg. Stock stays below shoulder/cheek; this reads as contact rather than shouldered shooting.
Withdrawal/recovery brings the stock and hands toward the belt; stance and weapon angle differ from guard and thrust without apparent head/boot scale change.
Horizontal high parry above the cap with two separated grips and two visible arms. The elevated weapon does not establish facing; head, trunk and feet retain SE bearing.

cellObservations.observation: SE hit/stumble with open balancing hand, slanted lowered stock and one main planted boot. Head/roll/boot proportions remain coherent with the contact kit; projected span is naturally longer than the crouched contact phases.
Knee-down with one open hand descending toward ground and the other holding a lowering rifle. The cheek is not set into a firing sight line.
Collapse is supported at the folded knee/hip and bracing hand, rifle falling across the body; raised rear boot does not define ground.
Final side/prone rest has head settled onto forearms and a released lowered rifle in front. Hands are relaxed and do not form an aiming support.

cellObservations.observation: Rear NW three-quarter guard with lowered rifle. Left canteen, brown rear pouch and strapped blanket/pack preserve the actual B NW kit arrangement.
Low-stock lunge with bent lead knee, rear toe support and separated hand grips. Weapon is clear of cheek and shoulder; extension and body weight distinguish it from the firing reference.

Recovery draws the rifle upward across the chest and hands closer to the body. An isolated still has ready-like ambiguity, but it is visibly distinct from the low lunge and high block; no sustained firing pose is asserted.
Raised two-hand parry with clear arm separation and NW-facing head/back/feet. Rifle is diagonally high rather than a literal horizontal bar; the frame reads as a block rather than aim.

groundMethods: Projected pelvis X follows the rear belt/crotch axis of the stumble; Y is the alpha>=64 maximum exclusive Y of the planted screen-left boot outsole. The lifted rear boot and released rifle are excluded.
Projected pelvis X follows the rear hip beneath the belt; Y is the alpha>=64 maximum exclusive Y of the folded supporting knee region. Both upturned boot soles and the low rifle are excluded.

Projected pelvis X follows the side/rear hip under the belt and pouch; Y is the alpha>=64 maximum exclusive Y of the load-bearing folded knee/hip region. Raised boot soles, forearms and rifle do not set this ground.

Projected hip X follows the side-rest pelvis beneath the rear pouch; Y is the alpha>=64 maximum exclusive Y of the resting folded thigh/knee region. Upturned soles and the separate dropped rifle are excluded.

cellObservations.observation: NW hit/stumble releases the musket and opens the hands; the nearer boot remains planted while the rear foot lifts. Cap, roll/pack and boot scale now match the contact partner sufficiently for this opt-in pair.

Knee-down lowers the body onto folded knees, with both boot soles lifted toward the viewer. The low rifle is clear of the cheek; the nearer wrist is partly occluded near its stock, so no finger/grip certification is made.
Collapse lowers the trunk with bent elbows and tucked legs, the musket separately down beside the body. Head/pack proportions remain coherent with the other source cells.

Final rest lowers the head toward the forearms with the rifle separate on the ground. No cheek-supported stock or raised aiming barrel remains; hips/knees support the body while soles remain upturned.

limitations: This accepts only the exact four source PNGs and independently bound registrations for the opt-in candidate. Public exports, runtime installation, default art, upload and final browser acceptance are separate.

Model-assisted source inspection is not human, anatomical or historical-drill certification. Fingers, rear grips and the knee-down NW wrist are partly obscured; each still cannot prove mechanical force or a complete real-world drill.

Contact lunges/parries and falling poses have intentionally different projected spans. Part comparisons support a bounded visual judgment, not physical scale metrology. Narrow parry cap ROIs exclude adjacent weapon/hand silhouettes, with ordinary one-pixel semantic boundary uncertainty.
Colored low-alpha fringes and nonzero edge noise remain. No fringe-free claim is made; actual terrain/zoom/crowding checks remain necessary.
This adds only Union B SE/NW contact/casualty. Other B bearings and existing movement coverage gaps remain; the family is incomplete. No whole-game grade, full-motion or GPU/device certification.
